#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: resume rehydrates completed-stage artifacts from the git state branch
# before the dispatch loop. (issue #1805, ADR-006 §3.5)
#
# SPEC-1 [code]: on resume, runner calls _artifact_persist_restore +
#   _artifact_persist_put_back and places completed-stage artifacts into
#   ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR before the dispatch loop; the complete stage emits
#   no stage.start event.
#
# SPEC-2 [code]: a complete stage whose primary artifact is absent from both
#   disk and the git state branch causes the resume to exit 1 before any
#   stage.start event is emitted.
#
# SPEC-5 [no-code]: ADR-006-resume-contract.md amended with step 3.5:
#   before the dispatch loop the runner restores completed-stage artifacts from
#   the git state branch; a still-absent artifact causes exit 1; enforcing
#   test names added inline.
#
# SPEC-6 [no-code]: ADR-050-prior-work-reuse-contract.md §6 amended with
#   boundary note: the invariant applies to new runs; a resume continues the
#   same run and is governed by ADR-006.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
ZBUILD_CLI="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/zbuild"
ADR_006="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-006-resume-contract.md"
ADR_050="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-050-prior-work-reuse-contract.md"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/state/artifact-persist.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/artifact-persist.sh"

print_test_header "resume-rehydrate — artifact restore on resume (#1805)"
setup_test_env "resume-rehydrate-1805"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

_ZB_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"

# ── Shared infrastructure ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Create a git repo that the runner will use (CWD of the subprocess).
# The state branch is written here; the runner also reads from here.
WORK_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo resume-rehydrate-work)"
git -C "$WORK_REPO" config user.email t@e.st
git -C "$WORK_REPO" config user.name t

install_template_overlay "$WORK_REPO" runner-state-dir-minimal

# Create mock plugins (intake + build, each declaring a primary artifact).
mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"

# ── SPEC-1: resume rehydrates artifacts from git state branch ─────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-1] resume restores completed-stage artifact into ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR"

S1_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s1-state"
S1_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s1-events"
S1_EVENTS_JSONL="$S1_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
S1_STATE_FILE="$S1_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
mkdir -p "$S1_STATE_DIR/artifacts" "$S1_EVENTS_DIR"

# Write the intake primary artifact so the snapshot captures it.
printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"prior-run intake"}' \
    > "$S1_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

# Snapshot the artifact onto the state branch in WORK_REPO.
_s1_snap_rc=0
( export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$S1_STATE_DIR"
  cd "$WORK_REPO" && _artifact_persist_snapshot "$S1_STATE_DIR" "$_ZB_ID" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s1-snap.log" 2>&1 || _s1_snap_rc=$?
if [[ "$_s1_snap_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1805/SPEC-1] setup: snapshot to state branch failed" \
        "rc=$_s1_snap_rc; $(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s1-snap.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -5)"
else
    assert_pass "[#1805/SPEC-1] setup: state branch populated with intake-result.json"
fi

# Remove the artifact from disk to simulate the "artifacts not on disk" scenario.
rm -f "$S1_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

# Write state file: intake=complete, build=pending.
jq -n \
    --arg run_id "s1-resume-1805" \
    --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
    --argjson issue "$_ZB_ID" \
    '{
        schema_version: 1,
        run_id: $run_id,
        issue: $issue,
        stage_statuses: {intake: "complete", build: "pending"},
        current_iteration: 0,
        self_heal_count: {},
        scope_manifest_hash: "",
        cost_ledger_pointer: 0,
        claim_lease_id: "",
        plugin_state: {},
        status: "in_progress",
        updated_at: $now
    }' > "$S1_STATE_FILE"

# Run runner --resume. CWD=WORK_REPO so _artifact_persist_restore finds the
# state branch. Capture rc; do not abort on failure.
set +e
( cd "$WORK_REPO" && env \
    ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 \
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT" \
    ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$S1_STATE_DIR" \
    ZBUILD_STATE_FILE="$S1_STATE_FILE" \
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$S1_EVENTS_DIR" \
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$S1_EVENTS_JSONL" \
    ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json" \
    ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn \
    ZBUILD_VISION_GATE=off \
    PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" \
    bash "$RUNNER" --template runner-state-dir-minimal --resume --issue "$_ZB_ID" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s1-stdout.txt" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s1-stderr.txt"
_s1_rc=$?
set -e

# [#1805/SPEC-1]: artifact must be present in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR after resume.
# Before the change: no rehydration → file absent → FAILS.
# After the change: rehydration copies artifact from state branch → PASSES.
assert_file_exists "[#1805/SPEC-1] intake-result.json rehydrated into ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR" \
    "$S1_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

# [#1805/SPEC-1]: intake must NOT have a stage.start event (it was complete and skipped).
_s1_intake_starts=0
if [[ -f "$S1_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    _s1_intake_starts="$(grep -c '"type":"stage.start"' "$S1_EVENTS_JSONL" \
        | xargs | grep -c '^[1-9]' 2>/dev/null || true)"
    # More precise: count stage.start events whose data.stage == "intake"
    _s1_intake_starts="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="stage.start") | .data.stage // empty' \
        "$S1_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^intake$' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
fi
assert_eq "[#1805/SPEC-1] intake emits no stage.start (complete stage skipped)" \
    "0" "$_s1_intake_starts"

# ── SPEC-6: ADR-050 §6 amended with resume boundary note ─────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-6] ADR-050 §6 amended with boundary note distinguishing resume from new runs"

# Extract §6 from ADR-050: content from the "### 6." heading up to (not including) "### 7."
_adr050_s6="$(awk \
    '/^### 6\./{p=1} p && /^### [0-9]+\./ && !/^### 6\./{exit} p{print}' \
    "$ADR_050" 2>/dev/null || true)"

# [#1805/SPEC-6]: §6 boundary note must say the invariant applies to new runs
# and that a resume is governed by ADR-006.
assert_contains "[#1805/SPEC-6] ADR-050 §6 boundary note says invariant applies to new runs" \
    "$_adr050_s6" "new run"

assert_contains "[#1805/SPEC-6] ADR-050 §6 boundary note names ADR-006 as governing resume" \
    "$_adr050_s6" "ADR-006"

# [#1805/SPEC-6]: §6 must say "a resume continues the same run" (not just reference ADR-006).
# Before the doc change: clause absent → FAILS. After change: PASSES.
assert_contains "[#1805/SPEC-6] ADR-050 §6 boundary note says a resume continues the same run" \
    "$_adr050_s6" "continues the same run"

# ── SPEC-12: fresh (non-resume) run dispatches all stages ─────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-12] fresh non-resume run dispatches all stages (ADR-050 §6 new-run side)"

S12_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s12-state"
S12_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s12-events"
S12_EVENTS_JSONL="$S12_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"

_S12_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
S12_WORK_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo resume-fresh-work)"
# Use a cycle fixture so SPEC-12 and SPEC-13 use the same cyclic pipeline.
# artifact-snapshot-coverage has intake (leaf) + cyc (cycle); that satisfies SPEC-13.
install_template_overlay "$S12_WORK_REPO" artifact-snapshot-coverage
# cycled sub-stage of the cyc cycle declares roles:[builder]
mock_plugin_factory "cycled" "agent" 0 "" "builder" >/dev/null

# Fresh state: no completed stages. status=in_progress and no --resume flag →
# runner treats this as a new run; no stage should be skipped.
jq -n \
    --arg run_id "s12-fresh-1805" \
    --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
    --argjson issue "$_S12_ID" \
    '{
        schema_version: 1,
        run_id: $run_id,
        issue: $issue,
        stage_statuses: {},
        current_iteration: 0,
        self_heal_count: {},
        scope_manifest_hash: "",
        cost_ledger_pointer: 0,
        claim_lease_id: "",
        plugin_state: {},
        status: "in_progress",
        updated_at: $now
    }' > "$S12_STATE_FILE"

# Run WITHOUT --resume: a fresh (non-resume) run.
# Contrast with SPEC-1 where a resumed run skips complete stages.
set +e
( cd "$S12_WORK_REPO" && env \
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT" \
    ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$S12_STATE_DIR" \
    ZBUILD_STATE_FILE="$S12_STATE_FILE" \
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$S12_EVENTS_DIR" \
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$S12_EVENTS_JSONL" \
    ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json" \
    ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn \
    ZBUILD_VISION_GATE=off \
    PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" \
    bash "$RUNNER" --template artifact-snapshot-coverage --issue "$_S12_ID" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s12-stdout.txt" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s12-stderr.txt"
set -e

# [#1805/SPEC-12]: intake must emit stage.start on a fresh run (not skipped by
# rehydration, which only applies on resume). This pins the new-run side of the
# ADR-050 §6 boundary: the prior-work reuse invariant governs new runs; a resume
# (governed by ADR-006) is the only path that may skip complete stages.
_s12_intake_starts=0
if [[ -f "$S12_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    _s12_intake_starts="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="stage.start") | .data.stage // empty' \
        "$S12_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^intake$' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
fi
assert_eq "[#1805/SPEC-12] fresh run dispatches intake (not skipped; ADR-050 §6 new-run side)" \
    "1" "$_s12_intake_starts"

# [#1805/SPEC-12]: the cycled sub-stage must dispatch (cycle executed; no stage skipped).
# Before fix: ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 suppresses the cycle → cycled_starts=0 → assert_gt fails.
# After fix: cycles enabled, cycled sub-stage runs for the 1 configured iteration → PASSES.
_s12_cycled_starts=0
if [[ -f "$S12_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    _s12_cycled_starts="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="stage.start") | .data.stage // empty' \
        "$S12_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^cycled$' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
fi
assert_gt "[#1805/SPEC-12] fresh run dispatches cycled sub-stage (cycle ran; no stage skipped)" \
    "$_s12_cycled_starts" "0"

# [#1805/SPEC-12]: the cycle fixture used for this fresh-run sub-case contains type: cycle,
# establishing that the fixture IS a cyclic pipeline (satisfying the "same cycle fixture" clause).
_s12_fixt_content="$(cat "$REPO_ROOT/tests/fixtures/templates/artifact-snapshot-coverage.yaml")"
assert_contains "[#1805/SPEC-12] cycle fixture used in SPEC-12 fresh-run sub-case has type: cycle" \
    "$_s12_fixt_content" "type: cycle"

# ── SPEC-13: test uses a fixture containing a cyclic stage ────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-13] resume-rehydrate test uses a fixture containing a cyclic stage"

# [#1805/SPEC-13]: the fixture must contain type: cycle (satisfies "containing a cyclic stage").
# Already read into _s12_fixt_content above from artifact-snapshot-coverage.yaml.
assert_contains "[#1805/SPEC-13] resume-rehydrate fixture contains type: cycle" \
    "$_s12_fixt_content" "type: cycle"

# [#1805/SPEC-13]: a pipeline using that cyclic fixture was actually run in this test.
# _s12_cycled_starts was computed in the SPEC-12 section from the S12 pipeline run.
# Before fix: ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 → cycled never dispatches → 0 → assert_gt fails.
# After fix (cycles enabled, max_iter=1): cycled dispatches → assert_gt passes.
assert_gt "[#1805/SPEC-13] resume-rehydrate: pipeline with cyclic fixture was actually run (cycled dispatched)" \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: cycle orchestrator reads persisted current_iter and starts the
# iteration loop from that value (not 1) on resume. (issue #1805, ADR-006 §3.5)
#
# SPEC-7 [code]: Cycle orchestrator reads cycle_iterations[CYCLE_ID].current_iter
#   from persisted state at resume and starts the iteration loop from that value
#   (not 1); iter-1 complete stages emit no stage.start on resume into iter-2.
#   Its test must FAIL on the code as it was before this change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
FIXT="$REPO_ROOT/tests/fixtures/templates"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "resume-loop-state — cycle orchestrator resumes from persisted iter (#1805)"
setup_test_env "resume-loop-state-1805"

export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"
# shellcheck source=../lib/cycle-report-stub.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/tests/lib/cycle-report-stub.sh"

STATE_FILE="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"

# ── SPEC-7: cycle starts from persisted current_iter on resume ─────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-7] cycle orchestrator resumes from current_iter (not 1)"

# Seed minimal state file required by _cycle_state_init.
: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"

# Use zb_engine_loop_state to write one completed iteration (current_iter=1)
# into the state file. This simulates: iter-1 of the cycle has run and
# completed; the run was then interrupted before iter-2 dispatched.
# After the change the orchestrator will read current_iter=1 and start from
# iter-2 (current_iter + 1). Before the change it starts from iter=1.
zb_engine_loop_state "$STATE_FILE" "build-test" 1 5 "in_progress"

# Load the cycle template.
load_template "$FIXT/cycle-converges-iter2.yaml"

# Mock cycle_dispatch_stage: record the first iter dispatched, always pass.
# We record across all stages because the very first dispatch call reveals
# which iter the orchestrator started from.
_SPEC7_FIRST_ITER=-1
cycle_dispatch_stage() {
    local stage="$1" iter="$2"
    if [[ "$_SPEC7_FIRST_ITER" -eq -1 ]]; then
        _SPEC7_FIRST_ITER="$iter"
    fi
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
    return 0
}

# The report stub makes the test member report zero test failures (pass).
zb_stub_reports_tests test

# Run the cycle orchestrator against the seeded state.
# Before this change: loop starts at iter=1 → first dispatch is iter=1.
# After this change: loop reads current_iter=1 → starts at iter=2 → first is 2.
set +e
cycle_orchestrator_run "build-test" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE"
_s7_rc=$?
set -e

# [#1805/SPEC-7]: first dispatched iter must be 2, not 1.
# Before the change: _SPEC7_FIRST_ITER=1 → assert 2==1 → FAILS.
# After the change:  _SPEC7_FIRST_ITER=2 → assert 2==2 → PASSES.
assert_eq \
    "[#1805/SPEC-7] first dispatched iter is 2 (resumed from current_iter=1, not restarted from 1)" \
    "2" "$_SPEC7_FIRST_ITER"

# [#1805/SPEC-7]: no cycle.iteration.complete event for iter=1
# (the orchestrator never ran iter-1, so it emits no completion for it).
_s7_iter1_complete=0
if [[ -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    _s7_iter1_complete="$(jq -r \
        'select(.type=="cycle.iteration.complete") | .data.iter // empty' \
        "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^1$' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
fi
assert_eq \
    "[#1805/SPEC-7] no cycle.iteration.complete for iter=1 (iter-1 was already done before resume)" \
    "0" "$_s7_iter1_complete"

# ── SPEC-13: test uses a fixture containing a cyclic stage ────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-13] resume-loop-state test uses a fixture containing a cyclic stage"

# cycle-converges-iter2.yaml is loaded above via load_template and driven through
# cycle_orchestrator_run. Assert it contains type: cycle to formally pin the fixture
# contains a cyclic stage (as this test's SPEC-13 contract requires).
_s13_loop_fixt_content="$(cat "$FIXT/cycle-converges-iter2.yaml")"
assert_contains "[#1805/SPEC-13] cycle fixture used by resume-loop-state test has type: cycle" \
    "$_s13_loop_fixt_content" "type: cycle"

# Also assert the pipeline was actually run: cycle_dispatch_stage was invoked
# during cycle_orchestrator_run above, setting _SPEC7_FIRST_ITER from its
# initial -1.  A value > -1 proves the cyclic stage was dispatched.
assert_gt \
    "[#1805/SPEC-13] resume-loop-state ran the cyclic pipeline (cycle_dispatch_stage was invoked)" \
    "$_SPEC7_FIRST_ITER" "-1"

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: all three resume entry paths invoke _runner_resume_rehydrate before
# the dispatch loop. (issue #1805, ADR-006 §3.5)
#
# SPEC-9 [code]: All three resume entry paths (--resume flag to runner.sh,
#   auto-resume on detecting status=interrupted, zbuild pipeline resume
#   --run-id) invoke _runner_resume_rehydrate before the dispatch loop.
#   Its test must FAIL on the code as it was before this change.
#
# Three sub-tests, each with a separate work repo, state dir, and events dir:
#   Path 1 — bash runner.sh --resume
#   Path 2 — bash runner.sh (no --resume; state status=interrupted → auto_resume)
#   Path 3 — bash zbuild pipeline resume --run-id
#
# Discriminating assertion for all paths: intake-result.json is present in
# ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR after the runner call (artifact restored from state branch).
# Before this change: no rehydration → artifact absent → FAILS.
# After this change: _runner_resume_rehydrate restores it → PASSES.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
ZBUILD_CLI="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/zbuild"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/state/artifact-persist.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/artifact-persist.sh"

print_test_header "resume-entry-points — all resume paths rehydrate artifacts (#1805)"
setup_test_env "resume-entry-points-1805"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

# Common mock plugins for all three paths.
mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
# cycled sub-stage used by the artifact-snapshot-coverage cyclic fixture (SPEC-13 sub-case).
mock_plugin_factory "cycled" "agent" 0 "" "builder" >/dev/null
PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"

# ── Shared helper: set up a work repo with a state branch for one path ──────────
# Usage: _setup_path_state <label> <issue_id> → sets:
#   P_WORK_REPO, P_STATE_DIR, P_STATE_FILE, P_EVENTS_DIR, P_EVENTS_JSONL
_setup_path_state() {
    local label="$1" issue_id="$2"

    P_WORK_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo "ep-${label}")"
    install_template_overlay "$P_WORK_REPO" runner-state-dir-minimal

    P_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-state"
    P_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-events"
    P_STATE_FILE="$P_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
    P_EVENTS_JSONL="$P_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
    mkdir -p "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts" "$P_EVENTS_DIR"

    # Write the intake artifact so the snapshot captures it.
    printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"prior-run intake"}' \
        > "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

    # Snapshot onto the state branch.
    local _snap_rc=0
    ( export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$P_STATE_DIR"
      cd "$P_WORK_REPO" && _artifact_persist_snapshot "$P_STATE_DIR" "$issue_id" ) \
        >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-snap.log" 2>&1 || _snap_rc=$?
    if [[ "$_snap_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
        assert_fail "setup-${label}: snapshot to state branch failed" \
            "rc=$_snap_rc; $(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-snap.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -5)"
    fi

    # Remove artifact from disk; it now lives only on the state branch.
    rm -f "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"
}

# ── PATH 1: --resume flag to runner.sh ────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-9] path 1: bash runner.sh --resume restores artifacts"

P1_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
_setup_path_state "p1" "$P1_ID"
P1_WORK_REPO="$P_WORK_REPO"
P1_STATE_DIR="$P_STATE_DIR"
P1_STATE_FILE="$P_STATE_FILE"
P1_EVENTS_DIR="$P_EVENTS_DIR"
P1_EVENTS_JSONL="$P_EVENTS_JSONL"

jq -n \
    --arg run_id "s9-p1-resume-1805" \
    --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
    --argjson issue "$P1_ID" \
    '{
        schema_version: 1,
        run_id: $run_id,
        issue: $issue,
        stage_statuses: {intake: "complete", build: "pending"},
        current_iteration: 0,
        self_heal_count: {},
        scope_manifest_hash: "",
        cost_ledger_pointer: 0,
        claim_lease_id: "",
        plugin_state: {},
        status: "in_progress",
        updated_at: $now
    }' > "$P1_STATE_FILE"

set +e
( cd "$P1_WORK_REPO" && env \
    ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 \
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT" \
    ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$P1_STATE_DIR" \
    ZBUILD_STATE_FILE="$P1_STATE_FILE" \
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$P1_EVENTS_DIR" \
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$P1_EVENTS_JSONL" \
    ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json" \
    ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn \
    ZBUILD_VISION_GATE=off \
    PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" \
    bash "$RUNNER" --template runner-state-dir-minimal \
        --resume --issue "$P1_ID" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1-stdout.txt" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1-stderr.txt"
set -e

# [#1805/SPEC-9] path 1 assertion: artifact restored.
# Before change: no rehydration → file absent → FAILS.
# After change: _runner_resume_rehydrate restores it → PASSES.
assert_file_exists \
    "[#1805/SPEC-9] path 1 (--resume flag): intake-result.json restored from state branch" \
    "$P1_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

# ── PATH 2: auto-resume on detecting status=interrupted ───────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-9] path 2: auto-resume on status=interrupted restores artifacts"

P2_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
_setup_path_state "p2" "$P2_ID"
P2_WORK_REPO="$P_WORK_REPO"
P2_STATE_DIR="$P_STATE_DIR"
P2_STATE_FILE="$P_STATE_FILE"
P2_EVENTS_DIR="$P_EVENTS_DIR"
P2_EVENTS_JSONL="$P_EVENTS_JSONL"

# status=interrupted → get_resume_recommendation → auto_resume → resume_mode=true.
jq -n \
    --arg run_id "s9-p2-resume-1805" \
    --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
    --argjson issue "$P2_ID" \
    '{
        schema_version: 1,
        run_id: $run_id,
        issue: $issue,
        stage_statuses: {intake: "complete", build: "pending"},
        current_iteration: 0,
        self_heal_count: {},
        scope_manifest_hash: "",
        cost_ledger_pointer: 0,
        claim_lease_id: "",
        plugin_state: {},
        status: "interrupted",
        updated_at: $now
    }' > "$P2_STATE_FILE"

# No --resume flag: runner detects status=interrupted and auto-resumes.
set +e
( cd "$P2_WORK_REPO" && env \
    ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 \
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT" \
    ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$P2_STATE_DIR" \
    ZBUILD_STATE_FILE="$P2_STATE_FILE" \
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$P2_EVENTS_DIR" \
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$P2_EVENTS_JSONL" \
    ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json" \
    ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn \
    ZBUILD_VISION_GATE=off \
    PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" \
    bash "$RUNNER" --template runner-state-dir-minimal ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2-stdout.txt" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2-stderr.txt"
set -e

# [#1805/SPEC-9] path 2 assertion: artifact restored via auto-resume.
# Before change: no rehydration → file absent → FAILS.
# After change: auto-resume path invokes _runner_resume_rehydrate → PASSES.
assert_file_exists \
    "[#1805/SPEC-9] path 2 (auto-resume/interrupted): intake-result.json restored from state branch" \
    "$P2_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

# ── PATH 3: zbuild pipeline resume --run-id ───────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-9] path 3: zbuild pipeline resume --run-id restores artifacts"

P3_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
_setup_path_state "p3" "$P3_ID"
P3_WORK_REPO="$P_WORK_REPO"
P3_STATE_DIR="$P_STATE_DIR"
P3_STATE_FILE="$P_STATE_FILE"
P3_EVENTS_DIR="$P_EVENTS_DIR"
P3_EVENTS_JSONL="$P_EVENTS_JSONL"
P3_RUN_ID="s9-p3-resume-1805"

# status=interrupted so zbuild doesn't refuse (aborted requires --force;
# interrupted is accepted). zbuild changes it to in_progress, then runner sees --resume.
jq -n \
    --arg run_id "$P3_RUN_ID" \
    --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
    --argjson issue "$P3_ID" \
    '{
        schema_version: 1,
        run_id: $run_id,
        issue: $issue,
        stage_statuses: {intake: "complete", build: "pending"},
        current_iteration: 0,
        self_heal_count: {},
        scope_manifest_hash: "",
        cost_ledger_pointer: 0,
        claim_lease_id: "",
        plugin_state: {},
        status: "interrupted",
        updated_at: $now
    }' > "$P3_STATE_FILE"

# zbuild pipeline resume reads ZBUILD_STATE_DIR and finds the state file by run_id.
# It sets status=in_progress and calls runner with --resume.
# The runner's CWD must be P3_WORK_REPO so _artifact_persist_restore finds the branch.
set +e
( cd "$P3_WORK_REPO" && env \
    ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 \
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT" \
    ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$P3_STATE_DIR" \
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$P3_EVENTS_DIR" \
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$P3_EVENTS_JSONL" \
    ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json" \
    ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn \

    bash "$ZBUILD_CLI" pipeline resume \
        --run-id "$P3_RUN_ID" \

    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3-stdout.txt" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3-stderr.txt"
set -e

# Before change: no rehydration → file absent → FAILS.
# After change: zbuild pipeline resume → runner --resume → _runner_resume_rehydrate → PASSES.
assert_file_exists \
    "[#1805/SPEC-9] path 3 (zbuild pipeline resume): intake-result.json restored from state branch" \
    "$P3_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

# ── SPEC-13: test uses a fixture containing a cyclic stage ────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-13] resume-entry-points test uses a fixture containing a cyclic stage"

# Run a fresh pipeline against the cyclic fixture (artifact-snapshot-coverage) to
# demonstrate that this test file exercises a pipeline containing a cyclic stage.

main() {
    local issue="" goal="" dry_run=false template="simple"
    local resume_mode=false from_stage="" no_resume=false force=false
    # #963: self-host mode — redirect read-only contract-grammar libs to a
    # working-tree snapshot. Honors ZBUILD_SELF_HOST=1 (resolved after parse).
    local self_host=false

    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            --issue)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--issue requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }
                issue="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --goal)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--goal requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }
                goal="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --template)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--template requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }
                template="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --dry-run)    dry_run=true;    shift ;;
            --resume)     resume_mode=true; shift ;;
            --no-resume)  no_resume=true;  shift ;;
            --force)      force=true;      shift ;;
            --self-host)  self_host=true;  shift ;;
            --from-stage)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--from-stage requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }
                from_stage="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --help|-h)  _usage; return 0 ;;
            *) error "Unknown argument: $1"; _usage; return 1 ;;
        esac
    done

    # #963: ZBUILD_SELF_HOST=1 is equivalent to the --self-host flag.
    [[ "${ZBUILD_SELF_HOST:-0}" == "1" ]] && self_host=true
    # #2225: the run's resume intent reaches every stage as ZBUILD_RESUME —
    # 1 (reuse prior work) unless --no-resume, and ZBUILD_RESUME=0 in the
    # environment is the same as the flag. Each stage decides what reuse means
    # for it; hydrate restores nothing under 0.
    ZBUILD_RESUME="$(_runner_resume_intent "$no_resume")"
    export ZBUILD_RESUME
    [[ "$ZBUILD_RESUME" == "0" ]] && no_resume=true

    if [[ -z "$issue" && -z "$goal" ]]; then
        error "Must specify --issue <N> or --goal \"<text>\""
        _usage
        return 1
    fi

    # --from-stage is only valid in resume mode
    if [[ -n "$from_stage" ]] && ! $resume_mode; then
        error "--from-stage is only valid with --resume"
        _usage
        return 1
    fi

    local plugins_root="${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/plugins}"
    # #1614: fill the manifest cache HERE, in main()'s own shell. yaml_get was
    # 6,338 awk spawns per run (~13s of 27s); most call sites read it inside $( ),
    # and a cache written in a command substitution dies with that subshell — so
    # the fill has to happen in a shell that every later subshell descends from.
    # Cheap no-op when the cache is disabled or the root does not exist.
    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
    fi
    local state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-$HOME/.zbuild/state}}"
    # #887: when neither ZBUILD_STATE_DIR nor ZBUILD_STATE_FILE is set, a fresh
    # run roots its state under runs/<run_id>/ so concurrent runs never share a
    # state dir / artifacts. Explicit overrides (tests, CLI resume) win and skip
    # the re-root. Resolved here; applied once run_id is known (fresh-start block).
    local _state_is_default=false
    [[ -z "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}" && -z "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE:-}" ]] && _state_is_default=true
    local template_file
    # Per-repo overrides live under the target repo's working tree (#653/#724
    # Copilot finding): use $PWD, not $_ZBUILD_ROOT (the install tree).
    if ! template_file="$(resolve_template_file "$template" "$PWD" 2>&1)"; then
        error "$template_file"
        return 1
    fi

    # Cross-check: ZBUILD_STATE_FILE vs --issue (issue #296 Δ-4)
    # Placed before --dry-run so dry-run also surfaces mismatches.
    # Fail-closed on corrupt state files (rather than letting get_state_field
    # silently return its default and skip the check).
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE:-}" && -n "$issue" && "$issue" != "0" \
          && -f "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE}" ]]; then
        if ! jq empty "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            error "ZBUILD_STATE_FILE='${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE}' is not valid JSON; refusing to honor it alongside --issue $issue (fail-closed)"
            return 1
        fi
        local _existing_issue

# cycle_dispatch_stage hook — F1 uses the same per-stage path that the
    # legacy stage loop uses. Returns the stage's rc; the orchestrator owns the
    # iteration semantics. Sets _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT / _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS
    # so the orchestrator can score until/plateau/divergence.
    cycle_dispatch_stage() {
        local _cd_stage="$1" _cd_iter="$2" _cd_state="$3"
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT=""
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW=""
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS=""
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_REASON=""
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_DISPOSITION=""
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_REPORT="{}"
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_DATA_KIND=""
        local _cd_plugin_dir _cd_rc=0
        # #1783: refresh the contract-reader snapshot before EVERY member, so a
        # gate reads the lib copy build just wrote rather than the previous
        # iteration's. No-op unless this run edits one of those libs.
        _runner_refresh_contract_snapshot "$state_dir" || true
        # ADR-042: resolve role-then-id (uniform with leaf + parallel paths) so a
        # role-bound cycle member whose plugin id ≠ stage name resolves correctly.
        _cd_plugin_dir="$(resolve_stage_plugin "$_cd_stage" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        if [[ -z "$_cd_plugin_dir" ]]; then
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="error"
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW="error"
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="failed"
            # #2187 (ADR-054 §6a): the template names a stage no installed
            # plugin provides — the setup is wrong, which is `misconfigured`
            # (was `broken`, #1822). It halts the run either way.
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_DISPOSITION="misconfigured"
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_REASON="no installed plugin provides stage '$_cd_stage'"
            return 1
        fi
        # #1823 (ADR-054 §4): clear the throttle marker BEFORE dispatching, so a
        # marker found afterwards belongs to THIS member. A marker left by an
        # earlier stage would classify this member's unexplained failure as
        # `throttled`, and `throttled` retries — one rate limit would become a
        # retry loop on an unrelated defect.
        # #2439 (ADR-054 §6a): a stage whose outcome says retry is run again
        # inside plugin_hook_call, the one place every dispatch arm reaches;
        # what is read below is its last try.
        local _cd_manifest _cd_observation _cd_rate_limited
        _router_clear_throttle_marker
        # #2265: restore the CALLER's errexit, never force it on. A forced
        # `set -e` here undid the unit loop's `set +e`, so this function's
        # `return 1` ended the runner on the spot — every top-level stage
        # that failed died with no stage.fail and no pipeline.end (#1844 run
        # 37066147994's pr stage).
        local _cd_had_e=0; case $- in *e*) _cd_had_e=1 ;; esac
        # ADR-025 pre-flight at the hook call itself: a member that starts
        # after an abort is recorded does not make its model call (#1850 review).
        if ! _zbuild_check_abort; then
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="failed"
            return 1
        fi
        set +e; plugin_hook_call "$_cd_plugin_dir" run "$_cd_stage" "$_cd_state"; _cd_rc=$?
        [[ $_cd_had_e -eq 1 ]] && set -e
        _cd_manifest="$_cd_plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
        # #1823: read the RAW wait status once, here. The observation is the one
        # fact worth keeping across the narrowing — it separates a stage that was
        # killed from one that is defective, and it is knowable only here.
        dispatch_rc_observation_v _cd_observation "$_cd_rc"
        # An `if`, not `[[ ... ]] && ...`: under errexit a failing && list is the
        # last command in the list and DOES trip it. (#1822 review finding.)
        _cd_rate_limited=0
        if _router_throttle_observed; then _cd_rate_limited=1; fi
        # The readers below take the RAW rc. That is not an oversight: every one
        # of them only ever tests `rc -ne 0`, which is identical for a raw 10 and
        # a narrowed 1, so narrowing before them would change nothing. The only
        # consumer of the distinction is this function's RETURN value, so the
        # narrowing happens there — after the readers, at the bottom.
        # _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT holds the CLASSIFIED verdict (pass|warn|fail|
        # unknown + structural-failure pass-through) — used for .stage_verdicts
        # persistence (state_helpers.sh: verdict_class contract) and the
        # `stage.complete verdict=...` event emitted at runner.sh:1309 in the
        # `stage:*` dispatch branch. Mutating this to raw values like "approve"
        # would silently break the indicator-glyph + stage.verdicts contract.
        # The readers run in this shell and share one parse of the result
        # (ADR-065 §5, round 9: each was its own $( ) before).

            || _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="missing"

cycle_dispatch_stage() {
        local _cd_stage="$1" _cd_iter="$2" _cd_state="$3"
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT=""
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW=""
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS=""
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_REASON=""
        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_DISPOSITION=""

        # gate reads the lib copy build just wrote rather than the previous
        # iteration's. No-op unless this run edits one of those libs.
        _runner_refresh_contract_snapshot "$state_dir" || true

        # role-bound cycle member whose plugin id ≠ stage name resolves correctly.

            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW="error"

            # plugin provides — the setup is wrong, which is `misconfigured`
            # (was `broken`, #1822). It halts the run either way.
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_DISPOSITION="misconfigured"
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_REASON="no installed plugin provides stage '$_cd_stage'"
            return 1

        # marker found afterwards belongs to THIS member. A marker left by an
        # earlier stage would classify this member's unexplained failure as
        # `throttled`, and `throttled` retries — one rate limit would become a
        # retry loop on an unrelated defect.
        # #2439 (ADR-054 §6a): a stage whose outcome says retry is run again
        # inside plugin_hook_call, the one place every dispatch arm reaches;
        # what is read below is its last try.

    # passing it. The companion per-run allowlist (ZBUILD_SCOPE_ALLOWLIST, from
    # plan.files[]) is derived per-stage below via _runner_export_scope_allowlist,

    export ZBUILD_SCOPE_MANIFEST="$state_dir/scope-manifest.md"
    # #887: events must follow the (possibly per-run) state dir, else two runs'
    # events interleave in one events.jsonl. event-bus.sh defaults all three
    # vars to $HOME/.zbuild/state at SOURCE time, so for the per-run default we
    # must FORCE + export them (a plain :- would keep the stale flat value).
    # An explicit state dir respects whatever events location is already set.
    if [[ -z "$_ZBUILD_EVENTS_PINNED" ]]; then
        # Operator did NOT pin events → follow the resolved state dir. This
        # covers fresh per-run (state_dir=runs/<id>) AND resume (state_dir
        # re-derived from ZBUILD_STATE_FILE's dirname), so a resumed run's
        # events stay in its per-run dir instead of leaking to the flat default.
        export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$state_dir"
        export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$state_dir/events.jsonl"
    else
        # Operator pinned an events location → respect + export as-is.
        export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL
    fi
    # #2131: the run-status comment sidecar — after the events path is fixed,
    # before the issue lock (so it never inherits the lock fd), from the target
    # repo (the runner has not entered the worktree yet). Never on a dry run.
    if [[ "$dry_run" != "true" ]]; then
        _runner_status_comment_spawn "$state_dir" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" "$PWD"
    fi
    # #887: latest-run pointer so `zbuild resume --latest` / `--attach` resolve
    # the most recent per-run dir without a scan. Only for the per-run default
    # (never pollute an explicit/test state dir). Atomic swap via ln -sfn.
    # #141: the prefix test was `<state_root>/runs/`, which stops matching the
    # moment a run nests under its issue — so `--resume-latest` would silently
    # stop working. Gate on "this is the default per-run dir" instead of on one
    # literal shape, and keep the symlink itself at the state root where every
    # reader already looks for it.
    if $_state_is_default; then
        ln -sfn "$state_dir" "$(zbuild_layout_state_root)/latest" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: pipeline resume CLI + auto-resume policy (issue #225)
# Covers:
#   (a) get_resume_recommendation returns auto_resume for in_progress state < 24h
#   (b) returns fresh_start for complete
#   (c) returns manual_resume_only for aborted
#   (d) pipeline resume with staged state skips completed stages
#   (e) --force overrides aborted status
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../core/state/resume.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/resume.sh"

print_test_header "pipeline resume — CLI + auto-resume policy (#225)"

setup_test_env "pipeline-resume"

# #1921 follow-up: reserved test identity (zb_test_issue). These were real
# issue numbers; a run keyed to one writes fabricated prior work onto that
# issue's state branch. Only identity positions and the strings DERIVED from
# them are swept — a bare number elsewhere is not an identity.
_ZB_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
# Wave 12-E (#664): default is enforce. Stub plugins used here lack honest
# inputs/outputs blocks; opt out — this suite tests resume policy.
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
STATE_FILE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state/pipeline-state.json"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STATE_FILE")"

# ── Helper: write a minimal state file ───────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _write_state <status> [updated_at] [stage_statuses_json]
_write_state() {
    local status="$1"
    local updated_at="${2:-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)}"
    local stage_statuses_json="${3:-{\}}"
    # Build JSON without passing stage_statuses as argjson to avoid shell quoting issues
    jq -n \
        --arg status "$status" \
        --arg updated_at "$updated_at" \
        --argjson _ZB_ID "$_ZB_ID" \
        '{
            schema_version: 1,
            run_id: "test-run-225",
            issue: $_ZB_ID,
            stage_statuses: {},
            current_iteration: 0,
            self_heal_count: {},
            scope_manifest_hash: "",
            cost_ledger_pointer: 0,
            claim_lease_id: "",
            plugin_state: {},
            status: $status,
            updated_at: $updated_at
        }' > "$STATE_FILE"
    # Merge stage_statuses separately if provided
    if [[ "$stage_statuses_json" != "{}" && "$stage_statuses_json" != '{\}' ]]; then
        local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp)"
        jq --argjson ss "$stage_statuses_json" '.stage_statuses = $ss' "$STATE_FILE" > "$tmp"
        mv "$tmp" "$STATE_FILE"
    fi
}

# ─── (a) auto_resume for in_progress < 24h ──────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: in_progress < 24h"

_write_state "in_progress" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
assert_eq "in_progress recent → auto_resume" "auto_resume" "$result"

# ─── (b) fresh_start for complete ───────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: complete"

_write_state "complete"
result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
assert_eq "complete → fresh_start" "fresh_start" "$result"

# ─── (c) manual_resume_only for aborted ─────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: aborted"

_write_state "aborted"
result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
assert_eq "aborted → manual_resume_only" "manual_resume_only" "$result"

# ─── (b2) fresh_start when no state file ────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: no state file"

rm -f "$STATE_FILE"
result="$(get_resume_recommendation "$STATE_FILE")"
assert_eq "no state file → fresh_start" "fresh_start" "$result"

# ─── (a2) manual_resume_only for in_progress > 24h ──────────────────────────
print_test_section "get_resume_recommendation: in_progress > 24h"

# ─── _runner_resume_rehydrate <issue> <state_dir> (#1805, ADR-006 §3.6) ─────
# Restore completed-stage artifacts from the git state branch into the
# artifact area before the dispatch loop runs. Non-fatal on restore failure;
# a still-absent artifact is caught by the dispatch loop's stale-artifact
# check which now exits 1 instead of warning-and-continuing (SPEC-2 / SPEC-9).
_runner_resume_rehydrate() {
    local _rr_issue="$1" _rr_state_dir="$2"
    local _rr_artifacts_dir="$_rr_state_dir/artifacts"
    local _rr_staging="$_rr_state_dir/resume-rehydrate.staging"
    rm -rf "$_rr_staging" 2>/dev/null || true
    _artifact_persist_restore "$_rr_issue" "$_rr_staging" || {
        rm -rf "${_rr_staging:?}" 2>/dev/null || true
        return 0
    }
    if [[ -d "$_rr_staging/artifacts" ]]; then
        _artifact_persist_put_back "$_rr_staging/artifacts" "$_rr_artifacts_dir" || true
    fi
    rm -rf "${_rr_staging:?}" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_from_stage_preflight <stages_arr> <from_stage> <state_dir> <plugins_root> ─
# For --from-stage <s>: restore + put_back artifacts from the git state branch,
# then verify every stage before <s> has its primary artifact in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR.
# Exits 1 naming the missing stage in stderr. (SPEC-3, SPEC-4, ADR-006 §3.6)
_runner_from_stage_preflight() {
    local -n _fsp_stages="$1"
    local _fsp_from_stage="$2" _fsp_state_dir="$3" _fsp_plugins_root="$4"
    local _fsp_artifacts_dir="$_fsp_state_dir/artifacts"
    local _fsp_staging="$_fsp_state_dir/from-stage-preflight.staging"
    rm -rf "$_fsp_staging" 2>/dev/null || true
    # Restore + put_back (same sequence as _runner_resume_rehydrate)
    _artifact_persist_restore "$_runner_issue" "$_fsp_staging" || true
    if [[ -d "$_fsp_staging/artifacts" ]]; then
        _artifact_persist_put_back "$_fsp_staging/artifacts" "$_fsp_artifacts_dir" || true
    fi
    rm -rf "${_fsp_staging:?}" 2>/dev/null || true
    # Verify every stage before the target has its primary artifact
    local _fsp_s _fsp_plugin_dir _fsp_manifest _fsp_prim_path _fsp_resolved
    for _fsp_s in "${_fsp_stages[@]}"; do
        [[ "$_fsp_s" == "$_fsp_from_stage" ]] && break
        _fsp_plugin_dir=""; _fsp_manifest=""; _fsp_prim_path=""; _fsp_resolved=""
        _fsp_plugin_dir="$(_find_plugin_for_stage "$_fsp_s" "$_fsp_plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        [[ -z "$_fsp_plugin_dir" ]] && continue
        _fsp_manifest="$_fsp_plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
        _fsp_prim_path="$(_verdict_primary_output_path "$_fsp_manifest" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        [[ -z "$_fsp_prim_path" ]] && continue
        _fsp_resolved="$(_verdict_resolve_path "$_fsp_prim_path" "$_fsp_state_dir")"
        if [[ ! -s "$_fsp_resolved" ]]; then
            echo "error: --from-stage '$_fsp_from_stage': stage '$_fsp_s' has no restorable primary artifact" >&2
            return 1
        fi
    done
    return 0
}

main() {
    local issue="" goal="" dry_run=false template="simple"
    local resume_mode=false from_stage="" no_resume=false force=false
    # #963: self-host mode — redirect read-only contract-grammar libs to a
    # working-tree snapshot. Honors ZBUILD_SELF_HOST=1 (resolved after parse).
    local self_host=false

    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            --issue)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--issue requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }
                issue="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --goal)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--goal requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }

        # consecutive stages don't render flush against each other. The
        # divider itself already prints a leading \n; this additional blank
        # gives the operator a clear vertical break between the previous
        # stage's `── end stage-io: <prev> ──` line (or any post-loop warns)
        # and the next stage's `━━━ <stage> ━━━` boundary. Wave 11B.
        printf '\n' >&2

        _render_stage_divider "$stage"

        # #508: append "  (started HH:MM:SS UTC)" in DIM. Two-space separator
        # before the paren matches the metadata-trailer convention used by
        # stage-io banner footers. Timestamp text stays outside the color
        # escape so NO_COLOR strips ANSI but preserves the timestamp.
        local _sc_ts; _sc_ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
        echo -e "${CYAN}${BOLD}▸${RESET} Running stage: ${_sc_color}${BOLD}${stage}${RESET}  ${DIM}(started ${_sc_ts})${RESET}" >&2

# _verdict_resolve_path_v <var> <raw> <state_dir> — the same, into <var>, with no
# subshell (ADR-065 §5).
_verdict_resolve_path_v() {
    local _vrv_out="$1" _vrv_raw="$2" _vrv_sd="$3"
    local _vrv_ad="${_vrv_sd}/artifacts"
    local _vrv_p="$_vrv_raw"
    _vrv_p="${_vrv_p//\$\{state_dir\}/$_vrv_sd}"
    _vrv_p="${_vrv_p//\$\{artifact_dir\}/$_vrv_ad}"
    _vrv_p="${_vrv_p//\$\{artifacts_dir\}/$_vrv_ad}"
    _vrv_p="${_vrv_p//\$\{stage_io_dir\}/$_vrv_ad/stage-io}"
    # run_id is interpolated into a path: strip anything but the sanitized set
    # the runner itself guarantees, so a hostile value cannot traverse.
    local _vrv_rid="${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}"; _vrv_rid="${_vrv_rid//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/_}"
    _vrv_p="${_vrv_p//\$\{run_id\}/$_vrv_rid}"
    # #2270: a map element's own name, so parallel elements never share a file.

# fixture (runner-state-dir-minimal.yaml: two leaf stages intake → build)
# installed as a per-repo `.zbuild/templates/` overlay (#1270) and run the runner
# with CWD = that repo, replacing the retired `--template standard` (#979). The
# prior version registered the full 14-stage standard roster and marked 13 stages
# complete + one (review) pending; the behavior is stage-count-independent, so we
# mark intake=complete + build=pending and re-point the "remaining stage" assertion
# from `review` to `build`.
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
INT_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/int_plugins"
INT_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/int_state"
INT_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/int_events"
mkdir -p "$INT_PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake" "$INT_PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build" \
         "$INT_STATE_DIR" "$INT_EVENTS_DIR"

# The fixture's two leaf stages both succeed. #1850/#2366: each declares result
# contract 3 and a JSON primary, and writes a contract-3 pass there.
for _plugin in intake build; do
    _fn="${_plugin//-/_}_run"
    cat > "$INT_PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/$_plugin/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
id: $_plugin
name: Test $_plugin
kind: agent
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: ${_fn}
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
provides:
  result_contract: 3
outputs:
  - id: ${_fn}_result
    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_plugin}-result.json
    type: ${_plugin}-result.json@1
    format: json
    required: true
    primary: true
EOF
    cat > "$INT_PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/$_plugin/plugin.sh" <<EOF
${_fn}() {
    local _art; _art="\${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-\$(dirname "\$2")/artifacts}"
    mkdir -p "\$_art"
    printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' \\
        > "\$_art/${_plugin}-result.json"
    return 0
}
EOF
done

# #1270: per-repo overlay repo; the runner resolves the fixture from CWD=$PWD.

# ADR-011 (pluggable orch backend)
set -euo pipefail

_RUNNER_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"

  --force           Resume even if status=aborted
  --self-host       Dogfood zBuild's own engine: redirect read-only contract-
                    grammar libs to a working-tree snapshot (#963, ADR-023)

Environment:
  ZBUILD_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE  Force a single platform; detection short-circuits.
  ZBUILD_SCOPE_PATHS        Newline-delimited scope paths; written as '+ <path>' entries.
  ZBUILD_SELF_HOST          Set to 1 to enable self-host mode (same as --self-host).
  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR   Override dir contract-reader stages source grammar libs from.
EOF
}

# Helpers extracted to dispatch.sh / state_helpers.sh in #279:
#   _find_plugin_for_stage       → core/pipeline/dispatch.sh
#   write_scope_override
#   _update_stage_status         } → core/pipeline/state_helpers.sh
#   _set_pipeline_status
#   (+ their _zbuild_runner_set_* jq filter helpers)

# Globals (not local) so EXIT trap can read them after main() returns.
_runner_run_id="" _runner_issue="" _runner_ended=false _runner_state_file=""
# ADR-054 §11 (#1944): run-level watchdog globals — PID of the watchdog background
# subshell (killed by the EXIT trap on clean exit) and the resolved limit in seconds.
_RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID=""
_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
# #1878: last reported snapshot-failure reason, so a static precondition is
# reported once rather than once per stage boundary.
_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON=""

# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
    _runner_ended=true
    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
    case "$v" in
        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
    _runner_ended=true
    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_note_push_failure <stage> (#2187) ───────────────────────────────
# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
_runner_note_push_failure() {
    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
}

# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. No changes, no save: only
# when HEAD carries commits past the commit the run started from, which the
# engine sets before any stage (#2367; #1801 run 38290215955: the end of hydrate
# force-pushed main over the branch's earlier work). Advisory: a failure is
# reported, never fatal.
_runner_push_work_branch() {
    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    local _base="${ZBUILD_RUN_START_COMMIT:-}" _ahead
    [[ -n "$_base" ]] || return 0
    _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
    local _err
    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
        return 0
    fi
    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
    local _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch="${ZBUILD_RUN_BRANCH:-}"
    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
        reattached)
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
        diverged)
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
    esac
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
# never blocks a run.
#
# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
# item 1 of #1807.
#
# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
# and leaving no trace anywhere.
_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
    # push had nothing to send.
    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0

    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
        saved)
            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
            ;;
        failed)
            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
            # no channel to surface on.
            #
            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
            fi
            ;;
        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
        *) : ;;
    esac
    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
    local _leak=""
    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
        # code commits still go to the work branch.
        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
    fi
    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
    return 0
}

# ─── stage-start time cache (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Populated immediately before _render_stage_divider for each stage; read at
# the ✓/✗ complete/fail sites to compute the duration suffix. assoc array so
# nested / out-of-order stages (none today, but safe) still resolve correctly.
declare -gA _RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS=()

# ─── pipeline-wide start time cache (#525) ───────────────────────────────────
# Populated once at the top of main() right after _runner_run_id is sanitized
# (well before the EXIT trap installs) so every pipeline.end emit site — incl.
# preflight failure (L289) and the EXIT trap — can render a duration. Empty
# until set; readers degrade to "?s" on cache-miss (mirrors _runner_duration_token).
_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS=""

# ─── _runner_now_ms (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;
# do NOT introduce a runner-specific override name). Non-numeric override is
# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.
_runner_now_ms() {
    local ovr="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE:-}"
    if [[ -n "$ovr" && "$ovr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$ovr"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"
        printf '%s' $(( 10#${us} / 1000 ))
        return 0
    fi
    printf '%s' "$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date -u +%s)} * 1000 ))"
}

# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
_runner_status_comment_reap() {
    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        local i
        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
            sleep 0.1
        done
        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
_runner_now_short() {
    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
        return 0
    fi
    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
    local out
    # The shell's clock, in UTC (ADR-065 §5); the date forms stay as the fallback.
    TZ=UTC printf -v out '%(%H:%M:%S UTC)T' "$sec" 2>/dev/null && [[ -n "$out" ]] && { printf '%s' "$out"; return 0; }
    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
    printf '%s' "$out"
}

# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
_runner_duration_token() {
    local stage="$1"
    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '?s'
        return 0
    fi
    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '?s'
        return 0
    fi
    local ms=$(( now - start ))
    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
    else
        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
    fi
}

# ─── _runner_export_scope_allowlist <state_dir> (ADR-043) ────────────────────
# Redaction by construction: the per-run scope allowlist, exported as
# ZBUILD_SCOPE_ALLOWLIST so route_to_model can redact without a plugin passing
# it. Called per-stage because nothing is reported before plan runs (empty then —
# harmless, the scope manifest is the base allowlist and this is purely ADDITIVE).
_runner_export_scope_allowlist() {
    local state_dir="$1"
    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" csv=""
    # #2189: the scope files stages REPORTED (plan reports its files) — the
    # engine no longer reads plan.json by path.
    if [[ -s "$rec" ]]; then
        csv="$(jq -r '(.scope_files // []) | unique | join(",")' "$rec" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
    fi
    # #1874: the shape floor is part of the scope — computed here, mechanically,
    # so build, redaction and shape-floor all read one list that already holds
    # the files a shape change owes. Memoised per scope: this runs every stage.
    if [[ -n "$csv" && "$csv" != "${_RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY:-}" ]]; then
        _RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY="$csv"; _RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV="$csv"
        if ! declare -F sf_scope_floor_files >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/shape-floor.sh
            source "${_ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib}/shape-floor.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        if declare -F sf_scope_floor_files >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            local -a _scope_arr=() ; local _ff
            IFS=',' read -r -a _scope_arr <<< "$csv"
            while IFS= read -r _ff; do
                [[ -n "$_ff" && ",$_RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV," != *",$_ff,"* ]] && _RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV+=",$_ff"
            done < <(sf_scope_floor_files "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}" "${_scope_arr[@]}" 2>/dev/null)
        fi
    fi
    [[ -n "$csv" ]] && csv="${_RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV:-$csv}"
    export ZBUILD_SCOPE_ALLOWLIST="$csv"
}

# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
_runner_record_report() {
    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
        sleep 0.05
    done
    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
    else
        rm -f "$tmp"
    fi
    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
#
# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
        return 1
    fi
    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
        return 1
    fi
    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
    #
    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
    #
    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
    # Measured before choosing the seam.
    #
    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
    fi
    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
    # an unchanged tree.
    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    fi
    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
    local _leaf _ok=1
    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
        esac
        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
            _ok=0
        fi
    done
    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
}

# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
#
# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
